cap.n0: DeepSeek shrank a model's memory of past words to 4 percent.|And it scored better.
cap.n1: Not worse: better, in their own tests at least. How?|With a vacuum pump, a pair of glasses and a luggage tag.|From Prof. Yufei Ding's CSE 291P, lectures 3 and 4.
cap.n2: Quick callback.|At the attention party, every token, a word or a piece of one,|carries a question card, its query;|a name tag, its key; and a parcel, its value.
cap.n3: The KV cache is the cloakroom:|a wall of tags and parcels for every earlier guest.|Last time, grouped-query attention let groups of heads,|the parallel copies of attention, share one rack.
cap.n5: This time the clerk packs.|This is multi-head latent attention,|from DeepSeek's V2 paper.|Instead of making heads share, it compresses.
cap.n6: The clerk puts a guest's tag and parcel|into one clear bag, and pumps the air out.|One flat pouch.
cap.n7: In the model, the pouch is a latent vector:|a short hidden summary, learned in training.|A learned matrix, W-down, squeezes the token into it.|Multiplying by a learned matrix is called a projection.
cap.n8: One pouch per token per layer,|holding both the key and the value.|Every head can get its own key and value back out of it.
cap.n9: How flat? In DeepSeek-V2 the pouch holds 512 numbers,|as long as four keys of 128,|against 32,768 for the keys and values of all 128 heads.
cap.n10: Where the picture stops:|a vacuum bag gives back exactly what went in.|This squeeze is learned,|and the model trains with it from the start.
cap.c4: It seems that pretty straightforward.|Like, what are the tricks here?|Why others cannot really think about it?
cap.n11: Here is the first catch.|To read a pouch, the clerk would unpack it:|two more learned matrices, W-UK and W-UV,|rebuild the name tag and the parcel.
cap.n12: And that for every earlier guest, at every new step:|the very work the cache was meant to save.
cap.n13: The way out is an optician.|How well the new question matches an old name tag|is a score: the key times the query.|And the key is W-UK times the pouch.
cap.n14: Matrix products can be regrouped:|the brackets move, the order stays.|Her slide calls it the associative property.|So W-UK can be multiplied into the query side first.
cap.n15: The optician grinds the unpacking|into the guest's glasses.|And the parcel's unpacking, W-UV,|folds into the output matrix,|the last multiplication, which mixes the heads' results.
cap.n16: The glasses are the same for every pouch on the table.
cap.c5: this is a loop invariant component.|You can abstract it outside of the loop.
cap.n17: The loop runs over every earlier token.|So the glasses are made once|per new token and head, not once per pouch.
cap.n18: And the guest reads|the whole row of sealed pouches through them.|Nothing is unpacked.
cap.c7: Does that solve all the problems?|No. Actually, there's a killer.|The killer is the positional encoding.
cap.n19: A model has to know word order.|RoPE, rotary position embedding,|is the usual way to mark it:|it turns each query and key by an angle|set by its position, like a clock hand.
cap.n20: Now every key is turned by its own angle,|after it comes out of the pouch.|In her derivation, that turn lands|between the question and W-UK,|and it is different for every earlier token.|Factors may regroup, but never swap places.|So no single pair of glasses fits them all.|Every key would have to be rebuilt again.
cap.n21: The fix: keep position out of the pouch.|The keys that come out of it are never turned,|so the glasses still fit.
cap.n22: Instead, each token gets|a small separate luggage tag, 64 numbers,|made from the token itself, turned by its position,|and cached beside the pouch.|Each head reads it|with a small turned piece of its question.
cap.n23: Her slide: separate what from where.|And one tag per token, shared by every head.|Her slide's reason:|where a word sits is the same for every head.
cap.n24: Now the size. Per token per layer:|the 512-number pouch plus the 64-number tag.|576 numbers, as long as four and a half keys.
cap.n25: A group keeps one key and one value, 128 numbers each: 256.|And 576 over 256 is two and a quarter.|So this is the cache of grouped-query attention|with just two and a quarter groups,|whatever the number of heads.
cap.n26: Her worksheet tries it on Llama 3's three shapes,|as if every head kept its own keys and values:|32 layers and 32 heads, 80 and 64, 126 and 128.
cap.n27: For the smallest, at two bytes a number:|36 kilobytes per token in her table, instead of 512.|Fourteen times smaller.|Then 28 times, and more than 56.|Even against Llama 3's real eight-group cache,|about 3.6 times smaller:|eight groups against two and a quarter.
cap.n28: And the quality?|In DeepSeek's own tests, at two model sizes,|the compressed version kept|4 to 14 percent of the cache,|and scored higher|on seven of eight benchmark scores.
cap.n29: Why would a squeeze help?|She offers guesses, and calls them guesses.
cap.c11: But if you really want to think|about why this is working,|I think it's kind of like why sometimes you do dropout.
cap.n30: Dropout:|switch off random parts of a network while it trains,|and it often does better.|A squeeze can be a trim that keeps the hedge healthy.
cap.c13: If it's working,|it means that there is some redundancy in it.|So you can do compression.
cap.n31: Plain attention may pack the same shirt many times over.|And keeping position apart|may stop it muddling the content.
cap.c14: But to me, I feel like a lot of this explanation|is still like we want to explain how it works.|No matter what kind of results we can get,|we always can find a reason for it.
cap.n32: These are the authors' own runs,|and their next report calls the quality|comparable to plain attention.|Their next model, V3, kept the design.
cap.n33: One last catch.|Inside attention, the glasses read every pouch whole:|512 numbers wide, where one head would read 128.|Several times more arithmetic|for every remembered token.
cap.c6: But the good news is for the serving process,|the memory overhead is a huge part.
cap.n34: Generating word by word, memory is the bottleneck:|a good trade.|But reading a whole prompt, the folded form|takes about three times the arithmetic.|So engines like vLLM switch:|unpack for the prompt, fold for generating.|Either way, the cache itself stays packed.
cap.n35: So: pack each token into one learned pouch,|and read it through glasses instead of unpacking it.|Keep position on its own small tag:|a cache the size of just two and a quarter groups.
